# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:36:59Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The deterministic-retry port has one blocking regression: the new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` is evaluated for every response in `SyncHttpClient._dispatch`, so a **successful 2xx/3xx whose body merely mentions "rate limit"/"throttl" is now retried** up to 5 times with backoff (~15 s+ wasted per call — e.g. Jira search results containing those words). Java only runs the body check on the exception path of failed requests; the old Dart code never retried 2xx. Verified live: `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit')` → `true`. Two minor items below do not block.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry` — success responses must be gated out before the body check (see inline comment)
- 💡 `_listDir` — `File(e.path).absolute.path` is not normalized; Java does `toAbsolutePath().normalize()` (see inline comment)
- 💡 test sorts a copy of the implementation's own output instead of pinning expected values

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false;` to `shouldRetry` and pin `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded') isFalse` in `deterministicRetryTests`
2. Normalize with `p.normalize(e.path)` (or trim the "normalized" wording)
3. Notes (no action required): lazy-tracker ticket item is verified by prose only — acceptable since `job_runner_test` already blanks `JIRA_*`; the Dart-side registry `FileTools.list` (`lib/src/integrations/file/file_tools.dart:296`) still returns unsorted, non-normalized entries — a parity gap if that path is ever served to agents; Java `listFiles` returns `null` for unlistable dirs while the bridge returns the `{"error": …}` envelope (pinned by the new test — a deliberate Dart convention, worth a one-line note in the test doc comment).

---

### Thread 2

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/sync_retry_policy.dart:181`**

🚨 **BLOCKING: successful (2xx/3xx) responses whose body mentions rate limiting are now retried**

`shouldRetry` is called from `SyncHttpClient._dispatch` for **every** response, including successful ones. The new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` drops the old implicit guarantee that only 429/502/503/504 were retryable, so any 2xx/3xx response with a body containing `rate limit`, `too many requests`, or `throttl` now returns `true`:

```dart
final p = const SyncRetryPolicy(maxAttempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 1000, ...);
p.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit'); // true — verified live
p.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled');             // true — verified live
```

This is a regression against both the old Dart behavior (a 200 was never retryable) and the Java port target: in Java `RetryPolicy.isRetryable(IOException)` (epam/dm.ai `dmtools-core/.../networking/RetryPolicy.java`) the body check only runs inside `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` — i.e. **only on the exception path of a failed request**; a successful response never reaches it.

Real-world impact: a Jira search/JQL call returning issues whose summary or description contains "rate limit" (very plausible — e.g. searching tickets *about* throttling) comes back 200 and is now re-issued up to 5 times with exponential backoff (~15 s+ of pure latency per call).

Fix — gate success responses out before the body check:

```dart
bool shouldRetry(int attempt, int statusCode, [String? body]) {
  if (!canRetryAfter(attempt)) return false;
  if (statusCode == 0) return true;
  if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false; // success: never retry
  return isRetryableStatus(statusCode, body);
}
```

And pin it in `deterministicRetryTests`:

```dart
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded'), isFalse);
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled'), isFalse);
```

---

### Thread 3

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/tool_bridge.dart:492`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: `File(e.path).absolute.path` does not normalize — comment and Java parity claim are off by one step**

The comment says entries are "absolute, normalized, and sorted", and the PR description claims parity with Java `FileTools.listFiles`. Java does:

```java
children.map(c -> c.toAbsolutePath().normalize().toString())
```

`toAbsolutePath()` alone does **not** collapse `.` / `..` segments — only `.normalize()` does. Dart's `File(...).absolute.path` likewise only prepends the CWD when the path is relative; it keeps redundant segments. So for an input like `outputs/../outputs` (or a symlinked working dir), Dart emits `…/outputs/../outputs/x` where Java emits the normalized `…/outputs/x` — a string-level parity gap for any caller diffing entries against Java output.

Note `_resolve` already guarantees the directory path is absolute before `listSync()`, so entries are effectively always absolute here already. Two cheap fixes, either of which restores the claim:

```dart
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;
// …
.map((e) => p.normalize(e.path))
```

(`p.normalize` also returns an absolute path here since `e.path` is absolute; using `FileSystemEntity`/`p` instead of `File(...)` also reads better for directory entries.)

Alternatively, if normalization parity is deliberately out of scope, trim the comment to "absolute and sorted" so the code doesn't over-promise.

---

### Thread 4

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart:37`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: ordering assertion would be stronger with known expected values**

```dart
expect(entries, orderedEquals([...entries]..sort()));
```

This verifies sortedness, but only against a copy of what the implementation produced — it can't catch a subtly wrong comparator or a sort applied to the wrong projection. The fixture creates exactly `b.txt`, `a.txt`, and `sub`, so the expectation can be pinned to concrete values:

```dart
expect(entries.map((e) => p.basename(e)),
    orderedEquals(['a.txt', 'b.txt', 'sub']));
```

(suffix sort happens to match basename sort here since all entries share the parent dir — or assert the full paths via `p.join(dir.path, ...)` for exactness.)

Real-world impact: a Jira search/JQL call returning issues whose summary or description contains "rate limit" (very plausible — e.g. searching tickets *about* throttling) comes back 200 and is now re-issued up to 5 times with exponential backoff (~15 s+ of pure latency per call).

Fix — gate success responses out before the body check:

```dart
bool shouldRetry(int attempt, int statusCode, [String? body]) {
  if (!canRetryAfter(attempt)) return false;
  if (statusCode == 0) return true;
  if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false; // success: never retry
  return isRetryableStatus(statusCode, body);
}
```

And pin it in `deterministicRetryTests`:

```dart
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded'), isFalse);
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled'), isFalse);
```"

The comment says entries are "absolute, normalized, and sorted", and the PR description claims parity with Java `FileTools.listFiles`. Java does:

```java
children.map(c -> c.toAbsolutePath().normalize().toString())
```

`toAbsolutePath()` alone does **not** collapse `.` / `..` segments — only `.normalize()` does. Dart's `File(...).absolute.path` likewise only prepends the CWD when the path is relative; it keeps redundant segments. So for an input like `outputs/../outputs` (or a symlinked working dir), Dart emits `…/outputs/../outputs/x` where Java emits the normalized `…/outputs/x` — a string-level parity gap for any caller diffing entries against Java output.

Note `_resolve` already guarantees the directory path is absolute before `listSync()`, so entries are effectively always absolute here already. Two cheap fixes, either of which restores the claim:

```dart

// …
.map((e) => p.normalize(e.path))
```

(`p.normalize` also returns an absolute path here since `e.path` is absolute; using `FileSystemEntity`/`p` instead of `File(...)` also reads better for directory entries.)

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:36:59Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The deterministic-retry port has one blocking regression: the new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` is evaluated for every response in `SyncHttpClient._dispatch`, so a **successful 2xx/3xx whose body merely mentions "rate limit"/"throttl" is now retried** up to 5 times with backoff (~15 s+ wasted per call — e.g. Jira search results containing those words). Java only runs the body check on the exception path of failed requests; the old Dart code never retried 2xx. Verified live: `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit')` → `true`. Two minor items below do not block.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry` — success responses must be gated out before the body check (see inline comment)
- 💡 `_listDir` — `File(e.path).absolute.path` is not normalized; Java does `toAbsolutePath().normalize()` (see inline comment)
- 💡 test sorts a copy of the implementation's own output instead of pinning expected values

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false;` to `shouldRetry` and pin `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded') isFalse` in `deterministicRetryTests`
2. Normalize with `p.normalize(e.path)` (or trim the "normalized" wording)
3. Notes (no action required): lazy-tracker ticket item is verified by prose only — acceptable since `job_runner_test` already blanks `JIRA_*`; the Dart-side registry `FileTools.list` (`lib/src/integrations/file/file_tools.dart:296`) still returns unsorted, non-normalized entries — a parity gap if that path is ever served to agents; Java `listFiles` returns `null` for unlistable dirs while the bridge returns the `{"error": …}` envelope (pinned by the new test — a deliberate Dart convention, worth a one-line note in the test doc comment).

---

### Thread 2

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/sync_retry_policy.dart:181`**

🚨 **BLOCKING: successful (2xx/3xx) responses whose body mentions rate limiting are now retried**

`shouldRetry` is called from `SyncHttpClient._dispatch` for **every** response, including successful ones. The new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` drops the old implicit guarantee that only 429/502/503/504 were retryable, so any 2xx/3xx response with a body containing `rate limit`, `too many requests`, or `throttl` now returns `true`:

```dart
final p = const SyncRetryPolicy(maxAttempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 1000, ...);
p.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit'); // true — verified live
p.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled');             // true — verified live
```

This is a regression against both the old Dart behavior (a 200 was never retryable) and the Java port target: in Java `RetryPolicy.isRetryable(IOException)` (epam/dm.ai `dmtools-core/.../networking/RetryPolicy.java`) the body check only runs inside `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` — i.e. **only on the exception path of a failed request**; a successful response never reaches it.

Real-world impact: a Jira search/JQL call returning issues whose summary or description contains "rate limit" (very plausible — e.g. searching tickets *about* throttling) comes back 200 and is now re-issued up to 5 times with exponential backoff (~15 s+ of pure latency per call).

Fix — gate success responses out before the body check:

```dart
bool shouldRetry(int attempt, int statusCode, [String? body]) {
  if (!canRetryAfter(attempt)) return false;
  if (statusCode == 0) return true;
  if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false; // success: never retry
  return isRetryableStatus(statusCode, body);
}
```

And pin it in `deterministicRetryTests`:

```dart
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded'), isFalse);
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled'), isFalse);
```

---

### Thread 3

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/tool_bridge.dart:492`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: `File(e.path).absolute.path` does not normalize — comment and Java parity claim are off by one step**

The comment says entries are "absolute, normalized, and sorted", and the PR description claims parity with Java `FileTools.listFiles`. Java does:

```java
children.map(c -> c.toAbsolutePath().normalize().toString())
```

`toAbsolutePath()` alone does **not** collapse `.` / `..` segments — only `.normalize()` does. Dart's `File(...).absolute.path` likewise only prepends the CWD when the path is relative; it keeps redundant segments. So for an input like `outputs/../outputs` (or a symlinked working dir), Dart emits `…/outputs/../outputs/x` where Java emits the normalized `…/outputs/x` — a string-level parity gap for any caller diffing entries against Java output.

Note `_resolve` already guarantees the directory path is absolute before `listSync()`, so entries are effectively always absolute here already. Two cheap fixes, either of which restores the claim:

```dart
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;
// …
.map((e) => p.normalize(e.path))
```

(`p.normalize` also returns an absolute path here since `e.path` is absolute; using `FileSystemEntity`/`p` instead of `File(...)` also reads better for directory entries.)

Alternatively, if normalization parity is deliberately out of scope, trim the comment to "absolute and sorted" so the code doesn't over-promise.

---

### Thread 4

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart:37`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: ordering assertion would be stronger with known expected values**

```dart
expect(entries, orderedEquals([...entries]..sort()));
```

This verifies sortedness, but only against a copy of what the implementation produced — it can't catch a subtly wrong comparator or a sort applied to the wrong projection. The fixture creates exactly `b.txt`, `a.txt`, and `sub`, so the expectation can be pinned to concrete values:

```dart
expect(entries.map((e) => p.basename(e)),
    orderedEquals(['a.txt', 'b.txt', 'sub']));
```

(suffix sort happens to match basename sort here since all entries share the parent dir — or assert the full paths via `p.join(dir.path, ...)` for exactness.)

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

- **State**: open

- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:36:59Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The deterministic-retry port has one blocking regression: the new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` is evaluated for every response in `SyncHttpClient._dispatch`, so a **successful 2xx/3xx whose body merely mentions "rate limit"/"throttl" is now retried** up to 5 times with backoff (~15 s+ wasted per call — e.g. Jira search results containing those words). Java only runs the body check on the exception path of failed requests; the old Dart code never retried 2xx. Verified live: `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit')` → `true`. Two minor items below do not block.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry` — success responses must be gated out before the body check (see inline comment)
- 💡 `_listDir` — `File(e.path).absolute.path` is not normalized; Java does `toAbsolutePath().normalize()` (see inline comment)
- 💡 test sorts a copy of the implementation's own output instead of pinning expected values

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false;` to `shouldRetry` and pin `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded') isFalse` in `deterministicRetryTests`
2. Normalize with `p.normalize(e.path)` (or trim the "normalized" wording)
3. Notes (no action required): lazy-tracker ticket item is verified by prose only — acceptable since `job_runner_test` already blanks `JIRA_*`; the Dart-side registry `FileTools.list` (`lib/src/integrations/file/file_tools.dart:296`) still returns unsorted, non-normalized entries — a parity gap if that path is ever served to agents; Java `listFiles` returns `null` for unlistable dirs while the bridge returns the `{"error": …}` envelope (pinned by the new test — a deliberate Dart convention, worth a one-line note in the test doc comment).

---

### Thread 2

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/sync_retry_policy.dart:181`**

🚨 **BLOCKING: successful (2xx/3xx) responses whose body mentions rate limiting are now retried**

`shouldRetry` is called from `SyncHttpClient._dispatch` for **every** response, including successful ones. The new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` drops the old implicit guarantee that only 429/502/503/504 were retryable, so any 2xx/3xx response with a body containing `rate limit`, `too many requests`, or `throttl` now returns `true`:

```dart
final p = const SyncRetryPolicy(maxAttempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 1000, ...);
p.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit'); // true — verified live
p.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled');             // true — verified live
```

This is a regression against both the old Dart behavior (a 200 was never retryable) and the Java port target: in Java `RetryPolicy.isRetryable(IOException)` (epam/dm.ai `dmtools-core/.../networking/RetryPolicy.java`) the body check only runs inside `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` — i.e. **only on the exception path of a failed request**; a successful response never reaches it.

Real-world impact: a Jira search/JQL call returning issues whose summary or description contains "rate limit" (very plausible — e.g. searching tickets *about* throttling) comes back 200 and is now re-issued up to 5 times with exponential backoff (~15 s+ of pure latency per call).

Fix — gate success responses out before the body check:

```dart
bool shouldRetry(int attempt, int statusCode, [String? body]) {
  if (!canRetryAfter(attempt)) return false;
  if (statusCode == 0) return true;
  if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false; // success: never retry
  return isRetryableStatus(statusCode, body);
}
```

And pin it in `deterministicRetryTests`:

```dart
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded'), isFalse);
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled'), isFalse);
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/tool_bridge.dart:492`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: `File(e.path).absolute.path` does not normalize — comment and Java parity claim are off by one step**

The comment says entries are "absolute, normalized, and sorted", and the PR description claims parity with Java `FileTools.listFiles`. Java does:

```java
children.map(c -> c.toAbsolutePath().normalize().toString())
```

`toAbsolutePath()` alone does **not** collapse `.` / `..` segments — only `.normalize()` does. Dart's `File(...).absolute.path` likewise only prepends the CWD when the path is relative; it keeps redundant segments. So for an input like `outputs/../outputs` (or a symlinked working dir), Dart emits `…/outputs/../outputs/x` where Java emits the normalized `…/outputs/x` — a string-level parity gap for any caller diffing entries against Java output.

Note `_resolve` already guarantees the directory path is absolute before `listSync()`, so entries are effectively always absolute here already. Two cheap fixes, either of which restores the claim:

```dart
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;
// …
.map((e) => p.normalize(e.path))
```

(`p.normalize` also returns an absolute path here since `e.path` is absolute; using `FileSystemEntity`/`p` instead of `File(...)` also reads better for directory entries.)

Alternatively, if normalization parity is deliberately out of scope, trim the comment to "absolute and sorted" so the code doesn't over-promise.

expect(entries, orderedEquals([...entries]..sort()));

expect(entries.map((e) => p.basename(e)),

`shouldRetry` is called from `SyncHttpClient._dispatch` for **every** response, including successful ones. The new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` drops the old implicit guarantee that only 429/502/503/504 were retryable, so any 2xx/3xx response with a body containing `rate limit`, `too many requests`, or `throttl` now returns `true`:

```dart
final p = const SyncRetryPolicy(maxAttempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 1000, ...);
p.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit'); // true — verified live
p.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled');             // true — verified live
```

This is a regression against both the old Dart behavior (a 200 was never retryable) and the Java port target: in Java `RetryPolicy.isRetryable(IOException)` (epam/dm.ai `dmtools-core/.../networking/RetryPolicy.java`) the body check only runs inside `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` — i.e. **only on the exception path of a failed request**; a successful response never reaches it.

```dart
bool shouldRetry(int attempt, int statusCode, [String? body]) {
  if (!canRetryAfter(attempt)) return false;
  if (statusCode == 0) return true;
  if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false; // success: never retry
  return isRetryableStatus(statusCode, body);
}
```

expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded'), isFalse);

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:36:59Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

  if (statusCode == 0) return true;
  if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false; // success: never retry
  return isRetryableStatus(statusCode, body);
}
```

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.
Now let me check tool_bridge.dart imports (does it import package:path?), and check the test file exists. Also check `_resolve`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 356
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/356
- **Title**: gh-349 parity: file_list/file_exists tools + lazy tracker in JSRunner + deterministic RetryPolicy (dm.ai#635)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-349` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +140
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T14:00:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T15:36:59Z

## PR Description

Closes #349
### What changed
Ported the deterministic-retry change from Java `RetryPolicy` (epam/dm.ai 3fa210e6, #635) and verified the other two items. `SyncRetryPolicy.isRetryableStatus`/`shouldRetry` now accept an optional response body: retryable by numeric status (429, 502/503/504) or a rate-limit/throttle body (`rate limit`, `too many requests`, `throttl`), never by substrings of an error message — the message embeds the request URL, so an ephemeral port like `50312` misfired the old `"503"` check and retried a 400. `SyncHttpClient` passes `resp.body` into the decision. Also aligned the JS-bridge `file_list` with Java `FileTools.listFiles` output (absolute, sorted `{"entries": [...]}`).

### Key decisions
- Ported the Java body-check branch exactly (case-insensitive, same three substrings); `statusCode == 0` stays an unconditional transport-failure retry.
- `file_list`/`file_exists` MCP catalog already matched the Java `@MCPTool` names/params — no catalog change; pinned the bridge behavior with `test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart`.
- Lazy tracker verified, no code change: `IntegrationClients` builds clients on first access (failure not cached); JS `jira_*` tools resolve config per call and fail on use with `Jira not configured` — `job_runner_test` runs scripts with all `JIRA_*` blanked.
- New tests mirror the Java `RetryPolicyTest` additions (URL port digits, retry by status/body).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/js/sync_http_retry_test.dart test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart
dart test            # full suite: 3646 passed, 16 skipped
crap4dart check --all  # 20 gates passed (coverage 96.7%), 1 pre-existing class_size warn
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[SyncHttpClient dispatch] --> POL[SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry]
  BODY[resp.body] --> POL
  POL -->|status 429/502/503/504| RETRY[retry with backoff]
  POL -->|body: rate limit / too many requests / throttl| RETRY
  POL -->|message/URL digits ignored| NORETRY[return response]
```
</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The deterministic-retry port has one blocking regression: the new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` is evaluated for every response in `SyncHttpClient._dispatch`, so a **successful 2xx/3xx whose body merely mentions "rate limit"/"throttl" is now retried** up to 5 times with backoff (~15 s+ wasted per call — e.g. Jira search results containing those words). Java only runs the body check on the exception path of failed requests; the old Dart code never retried 2xx. Verified live: `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit')` → `true`. Two minor items below do not block.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `SyncRetryPolicy.shouldRetry` — success responses must be gated out before the body check (see inline comment)
- 💡 `_listDir` — `File(e.path).absolute.path` is not normalized; Java does `toAbsolutePath().normalize()` (see inline comment)
- 💡 test sorts a copy of the implementation's own output instead of pinning expected values

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false;` to `shouldRetry` and pin `shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded') isFalse` in `deterministicRetryTests`
2. Normalize with `p.normalize(e.path)` (or trim the "normalized" wording)
3. ---

### Thread 2

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/sync_retry_policy.dart:181`**

🚨 **BLOCKING: successful (2xx/3xx) responses whose body mentions rate limiting are now retried**

`shouldRetry` is called from `SyncHttpClient._dispatch` for **every** response, including successful ones. The new body branch in `isRetryableStatus` drops the old implicit guarantee that only 429/502/503/504 were retryable, so any 2xx/3xx response with a body containing `rate limit`, `too many requests`, or `throttl` now returns `true`:

```dart
final p = const SyncRetryPolicy(maxAttempts: 5, baseDelayMs: 1000, ...);
p.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'docs about rate limit'); // true — verified live
p.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled');             // true — verified live
```

This is a regression against both the old Dart behavior (a 200 was never retryable) and the Java port target: in Java `RetryPolicy.isRetryable(IOException)` (epam/dm.ai `dmtools-core/.../networking/RetryPolicy.java`) the body check only runs inside `isRetryableStatus(RestClientException)` — i.e. **only on the exception path of a failed request**; a successful response never reaches it.

Real-world impact: a Jira search/JQL call returning issues whose summary or description contains "rate limit" (very plausible — e.g. searching tickets *about* throttling) comes back 200 and is now re-issued up to 5 times with exponential backoff (~15 s+ of pure latency per call).

Fix — gate success responses out before the body check:

```dart
bool shouldRetry(int attempt, int statusCode, [String? body]) {
  if (!canRetryAfter(attempt)) return false;
  if (statusCode == 0) return true;
  if (statusCode >= 200 && statusCode < 400) return false; // success: never retry
  return isRetryableStatus(statusCode, body);
}
```

And pin it in `deterministicRetryTests`:

```dart
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 200, 'rate limit exceeded'), isFalse);
expect(policy.shouldRetry(1, 302, 'throttled'), isFalse);
```

---

### Thread 3

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`lib/src/js/tool_bridge.dart:492`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: `File(e.path).absolute.path` does not normalize — comment and Java parity claim are off by one step**

The comment says entries are "absolute, normalized, and sorted", and the PR description claims parity with Java `FileTools.listFiles`. Java does:

```java
children.map(c -> c.toAbsolutePath().normalize().toString())
```

`toAbsolutePath()` alone does **not** collapse `.` / `..` segments — only `.normalize()` does. Dart's `File(...).absolute.path` likewise only prepends the CWD when the path is relative; it keeps redundant segments. So for an input like `outputs/../outputs` (or a symlinked working dir), Dart emits `…/outputs/../outputs/x` where Java emits the normalized `…/outputs/x` — a string-level parity gap for any caller diffing entries against Java output.

Note `_resolve` already guarantees the directory path is absolute before `listSync()`, so entries are effectively always absolute here already. Two cheap fixes, either of which restores the claim:

```dart
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;
// …
.map((e) => p.normalize(e.path))
```

(`p.normalize` also returns an absolute path here since `e.path` is absolute; using `FileSystemEntity`/`p` instead of `File(...)` also reads better for directory entries.)

Alternatively, if normalization parity is deliberately out of scope, trim the comment to "absolute and sorted" so the code doesn't over-promise.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-05):
📍 **`test/js/file_tools_bridge_test.dart:37`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: ordering assertion would be stronger with known expected values**

```dart
expect(entries, orderedEquals([...entries]..sort()));
```

This verifies sortedness, but only against a copy of what the implementation produced — it can't catch a subtly wrong comparator or a sort applied to the wrong projection. The fixture creates exactly `b.txt`, `a.txt`, and `sub`, so the expectation can be pinned to concrete values:

```dart
expect(entries.map((e) => p.basename(e)),
    orderedEquals(['a.txt', 'b.txt', 'sub']));
```

(suffix sort happens to match basename sort here since all entries share the parent dir — or assert the full paths via `p.join(dir.path, ...)` for exactness.)

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).
